patterns: what tools you used to build them
answers.answer: I build batch and streaming pipelines on Azure: Data Factory for orchestration, Databricks and PySpark for transformation, and Delta Lake in a bronze/silver/gold medallion layout. Recent work cut a nightly load from four hours to thirty-five minutes by repartitioning the silver layer.

My warehouse work is on Azure Synapse Analytics and Microsoft Fabric rather than Snowflake, Redshift or BigQuery. The modelling is the same — Kimball dimensional models, star schemas and semantic layers — but I would be learning those three products on the job.

Data Factory alerts on failed activity runs, Databricks job metrics feed a Log Analytics workspace, and each medallion layer carries row-count and freshness checks that fail the run rather than publishing bad data. On call, I triage from the failing activity's input snapshot.

I have not used dbt in production. My transformation layer is PySpark and Delta Live Tables, which covers the same ground — versioned models, tests and lineage — so the concepts transfer, but dbt itself would be new to me.

I run Structured Streaming jobs on Databricks reading from Event Hub into Delta tables, with watermarking for late arrivals and checkpointed exactly-once writes. Latency targets have been in the one-to-five minute range rather than sub-second.

Quality is enforced in the pipeline, not after it: schema contracts at ingestion, row-count and referential checks between medallion layers, and a scorecard published per layer. For compliance I have worked under SOX and HIPAA, using row-level security, data classification and retained audit trails.
